pr_title: Fix SQLite3 quoting to not put database and table in separate quotes
pr_body:
This reverts a fix that broke schemas in SQLite3, and applies a different fix to solve the same test case.

This fixes #35292.

Basically, when passing a symbol with a dot to `pluck`, we are expecting it to be a table + a column. MySQL and PostgreSQL handled it fine, because quoting `schema + table` is the same as quoting `table + column`: `"part1"."part2"`. So a quote_table_name was being applied by pluck.

However, this is not the case in SQLite3, which wants `"schema.table"."column"` (note the schema and table in the same quotes), and so would generate `"table.column"`. The applied logic is instead to check for a dot, and if found, to quote each part separately.
pr_comments:
Okay, so the root cause of all of this is absolutely bonkers. Nothing is what it seems and I was wrong. But the story is interesting.

TL;DR: Quoting schema/tables is the same in SQLite as the other databases. No weird need for ".", the fix is correct and just made my code start actually testing the right thing and find a subtle bug elsewhere. SQLite's Attached database was never actually supported, and supporting them appears not worth the trouble.

Because of the bad quoting that was going on before the fix, when my gem, in its tests, would create a table in a database (using `create_table "my_schema.thing" do ...`), the actual generated SQL would be a `CREATE TABLE "my_schema.thing"`). This is actually a table with a name that contain a dot, and not a table that refers to the schema.

Then, later on, the code in all my tests also also used the quote_table_name, and so everything always used a table_name with a dot instead of testing actual schemas.

What threw me in this weird quoting behavior understanding in 6.0 is that I would get syntax errors when trying to use the models. But that was not form the select or such things. No. It was from a call to PRAGMA which does things special for schemas (attached database). See, this is the query to get the table information in SQLite:

`"PRAGMA table_info(#{quote_table_name(table_name)})"`

However, when dealing with database, the actual syntax is

`"PRAGMA schema_name.table_info(table_name)"`

But those kinds of calls are not shown in the log, so I would get confused thinking the problem was in the previous query (because the problematic query is not shown in the error messages... which i don't know why).

Now that part could be fixed with some code to split the table name into schema + table in an intelligent way (so that quoted parts remain the same). But here is a the kicker:

In a `SELECT` in SQLite, you cannot specify the database at the attributes parts. Meaning:

`SELECT bar.id FROM foo.bar` is valid, but
`SELECT foo.bar.id FROM foo.bar` is not valid, its a syntax error!

So in order to generate correct queries here, things get even more wild. It's clear to me that this is not worth my trouble (or anyone's).

Sorry for the waste of time. Such a rabbit hole...

issue_context.title: SQLite no longer works when using table_name with a dot ex: "foo.bar"
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
The following fails on master.
[sqlite_master_demo.txt](https://github.com/rails/rails/files/2871394/sqlite_master_demo.txt)
But the same code ran against rails 5.2, and all version since 4, will pass:
[sqlite_521_demo.txt](https://github.com/rails/rails/files/2871396/sqlite_521_demo.-.Copy.txt)

Without using a complicated file (or creating any table), the following makes it easy to try:
```
class Post < ActiveRecord::Base
  self.table_name = "bar.posts"
end
Post.first
```
In 6.0.0, SQLite whines of a syntax error, while on 5.2.1, it whine of a table that doesn't exist (as expected).

### Expected behavior
When using a "schema" or an "attached database", (names change based on which DB), things normally just work by using a simple `self.table_name = "bar.posts"`. This is no longer the case for SQLite3 in rails 6.0.0.

For the example with Post.first above, the generated SQL should be:
`SELECT  "foo.bar".* FROM "foo.bar" ORDER BY "foo.bar"."id" ASC LIMIT ?`

### Actual behavior
Since 6.0.0, it now does:
`SELECT "foo"."bar".* FROM "foo"."bar" ORDER BY "foo"."bar"."id" ASC LIMIT ?`

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 6.0.0.beta1

**Ruby version**: 2.5.0

### More details
This is the PR that introduced this bug: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/34626
